candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall collect a minimum of three samples (flow-weighted composite if possible) from the outfall(s).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a minimum sample-count obligation at each outfall; whether 'flow-weighted composite if possible' is mandatory or discretionary affects which sampling method is required and whether observed sampling satisfies the obligation.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall collect a second and third sample (composite samples if possible) for use during the 24-hour renewal of each dilution concentration for each test.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Requires additional composite samples tied to dilution-concentration renewal during each toxicity test; interpretation of scope ('each test', 'if possible') changes whether extra sampling events are obligated.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee must collect the composite samples so that the maximum holding time for any effluent sample shall not exceed 36 hours for first use of the sample.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a 36-hour holding-time ceiling that can determine test validity; different readings of 'first use' or compliance with the ceiling change whether monitoring evidence is adequate or a result is invalid/missing.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee must have initiated the toxicity test within 36 hours after the collection of the last portion of the first composite sample.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Imposes a test-initiation deadline relative to sample collection; whether initiation met this window affects whether a toxicity test counts as valid and how missing or late-initiated results are classified.

candidates.exact_span: Samples shall be chilled to 6 degrees Centigrade during collection, shipping, and/or storage.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Prescribes sample-handling temperature; interpretation of compliance with chilling requirements can change whether samples and resulting tests are treated as valid monitoring evidence.

candidates.exact_span: A holding time up to 72 hrs is allowed upon notification to EPA and NMED of the need for additional holding time.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Creates a conditional extension of the default holding-time limit contingent on agency notification; whether notification occurred and was sufficient changes whether extended holding invalidates a test or excuses otherwise late use.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee must collect the composite samples such that the effluent samples are representative of the discharge duration, and of any periodic episode of chlorination, biocide usage or other potentially toxic substance discharged on an intermittent basis.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Conditions sampling on representativeness across discharge duration and intermittent toxic episodes; different interpretations of when intermittent discharges trigger capture requirements change applicable monitoring obligations and which effluent conditions are measured for limit comparison or deemed adequately documented.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall prepare a full report of the results of all tests conducted pursuant to this part in accordance with the Report Preparation Section of the most current publication of the method manual, for every valid or invalid toxicity test initiated, whether carried to completion or not.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines reporting obligations for all initiated tests regardless of completion or validity; scope of 'full report' and which initiated tests qualify affects whether missing documentation is a reporting gap or adequately explained.

candidates.exact_span: For any test which fails, is considered invalid, or which is terminated early for any reason, the full report must be submitted for agency review.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Imposes mandatory submission of full reports for failed, invalid, or early-terminated tests; interpretation of failure/invalidity/early termination changes whether agency-review reporting was required and how absent DMR results are classified.

candidates.exact_span: A valid test for each species must be reported during each reporting period specified in PART I of this permit unless the permittee is performing a TRE which may increase the frequency of testing and reporting.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a per-species, per-reporting-period valid-test requirement cross-referenced to PART I, with a TRE exception; whether TRE status applies and what PART I periods require changes obligated test frequency and whether a missing valid test is excused or unresolved.

candidates.exact_span: One set of biomonitoring data for each species is to be recorded on the DMR for each reporting period.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies DMR recording expectations per species per reporting period; interpretation of 'one set' and which results qualify as biomonitoring data affects whether reported data satisfy the obligation or leave a missing-evidence case.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall submit the results of each valid toxicity test on the subsequent monthly DMR for that reporting period as follows below.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Ties submission timing of valid toxicity results to the subsequent monthly DMR; different readings of reporting period alignment change whether a result was due on a given DMR and whether absence reflects late reporting or missing evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Only results of valid tests are to be reported on the DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Restricts DMR-reported results to valid tests only; interpretation of test validity therefore determines whether a numeric toxicity result is available for limit comparison versus classified as a non-reportable invalid outcome.
